Rewrote `mergeConfig` in `config.mjs` (named export unchanged).

What changed:
- **Validation**: both arguments must be non-null, non-array plain objects (prototype `Object.prototype` or `null`); otherwise `TypeError`. `overrides` still defaults to `{}`.
- **Own enumerable string keys only**: iteration uses `Object.keys`, so inherited keys are ignored.
- **Safe keys**: all writes go through `Object.defineProperty` (`setOwn`), so `__proto__` and `constructor` become ordinary own data properties — including when they come from `JSON.parse` — instead of mutating the prototype.
- **Merge semantics**: top-level keys merged with overrides winning; when both sides are one-level nested plain objects (values primitive), their own fields are merged with defaults preserved; otherwise the override replaces the value (so `false`, `0`, `null` win).
- **Freshness**: returns a brand-new top-level object with newly allocated nested objects; neither argument is mutated and no nested references are retained. Repeated calls with the same `defaults` are independent.

Not verified by execution: no shell/test runner is available in this environment, so I only reviewed the code by reading it back.
